gaps.criterion: Routing proposals are backed by simulation evidence
gaps.gap: THE GUARD IS PROVEN AND IS STRUCTURAL. RoutingRepair declares simulation as a REQUIRED field, so an unbacked repair is unconstructible rather than merely discouraged; routingRepairs() measures skew first, calls sdk-assignment second, and builds a proposal ONLY if the simulation returned. An executing test asserts that in the real unreachable state this suite runs in (no gateway configured): genuine skew is present, repairs is empty, and routingUnavailableReason is 'assignment_simulation_unavailable' so 'routing is healthy' stays distinguishable from 'we could not check'. The api_definition asserts the same over HTTP. WHAT IS UNPROVEN is the POSITIVE path: no sdk-assignment exists here, so a simulation has never actually returned and a backed RoutingRepair has never been constructed, proposed or reviewed. The criterion therefore holds today partly by vacuity — there are no routing proposals at all, so none lack evidence — and the branch that maps a real simulation response onto projectedShare/breachesBefore/breachesAfter has never executed. Closing it needs one run against a live sdk-assignment. NOTE a real defect found and fixed on the way, which would have made this silently vacuous forever: skew was measured as an absolute 15-percentage-point gap above fair share, which is unreachable on any real team — this project's own database has 2,969 owners, so fair share is 0.03% and triggering would have needed one person holding 15% of every open lead in the tenant. It is now a MULTIPLE of fair share (2x, floor of 5 open leads, worst 5 simulated per run), which means the same thing at any team size.
